body:
> At any rate, I don't see how you could avoid ostracizing the majority if
> you're going to tell them that no, they're not happy to have their own
> cars, television sets, and ready supply of processed foods - and that, in
> fact, you think the entire system which makes these things possible needs
> to be dismantled, and that many of them and their children need to die.

That depends on who this "majority" is. Naturally all of us (even
myself) would not be *happy* to have my food supply yanked & my kids
slaughtered tomorrow. 
Plus I'm sure that you could go into an audience of ignorant imbeciles
(out of the movie Fahrenheit 451, let's say) and say "Hey, those
enviro's are coming to cart away your TV sets!!" and incite mass
hysteria.


Nevertheless a lot of people with even limited intelligence realize that
this planet is headed for big trouble. If we could see into the future &
realize that our overpopulation & exploitation are heading us toward the
brink... many of us would prefer to cut back on our luxuries and
conserve now. People have accepted "inconveniences" and "sacrifices"
already (recycling, vegetarianism, environmental laws). People have
accepted the necessity for change... and our "leaders" and capitalist
Daddies have lagged behind. (You'd think that by now someone would have
marketed alternative energy equipment with the same enthusiasm as they
have marketed the better mega-software package of the month.) I think a
lot of us would accept cultural alternatives that would cut down on our
auto dependence & power consumption... but that would require
cooperation, not our culture's present worship of me-first materialism &
greed.

They would probably be more accepting of the planetary ethos if not for
the competing ethos of the capitalists that says "ME FIRST" and "MORE"
and tells them that "those environmentalists are a bunch of left-wing
wackos who are stealing our rights".

> 214. To avoid this, a movement that exalts nature and opposes technology
> must take a resolutely anti-leftist stance and must avoid all
> collaboration with leftists.

This is one of Ted's big mistakes. There is ALREADY a movement that
exalts nature & opposes tech. It's called EARTH FIRST! and it is NOT
"leftist". If anything, it is "pagan". Earth First! has been fiercely
defending Nature (see my earlier messages about the Tree Sitters) and
that has nothing to do with "leftism". Ted needed to get a clue. I'd get
him a subscription to Earth First Journal if I thought they'ld let him
have it.

> This leaves him open, primarily, to rightist revolutionaries and pure
> anarchists as members of his cadre;  the latter are in relatively short
> supply compared to the former.
> 
> There's a very interesting group of people, primarily artists by vocation
> rather than political sorts, with a useful take on modern society which
> is neither left nor right.  These folks are known as the Situationists;
> they probably reached their apex of influence during the uprising in
> Paris in 1968. 

Thanks, I have always been curious about them. And I think their
successor today is UNAPACK. One might call them "quality of life"
anarchists or Luddites. And I think their number is much larger than you
think, they are just unaware & unorganized. They are the people who say
"turn off the TV and refuse to buy the products".
If all of these people could become conscious of themselves and become a
movement... we'd see some big changes. Perhaps that should be our goal. 

Which brings me back to the original subject of this post: Luddite
poetry. "Live your life as an act of rebellion!"
